description: Erection of part single part two storey front extensions and a first floor extension to the existing place of worship to form an additional storey with a dome and minaret. The proposal includes associated cycle and bin storage and changes to the windows to suit internal re-modelling of the place of worship.
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin no later than three years from the date of this decision. 
Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The proposed development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in the application and the plans submitted (Design and Access Statement and Site Location Plan. Received: 24/12/2021. 74-76HIBERNIA/FP4 Rev 0, Events Schedule. Received: 21/08/2023. Car Paring Survey (2024). Received: 05/03/2024. 74-76HIBERNIA/FP1 Rev E, 74-76HIBERNIA/FP2 Rev D, 74-76HIBERNIA/FP7 Rev D, 74-76HIBERNIA/FP8 Rev B. Received on 07/07/2025. 74-76HIBERNIA/FP6 Rev F, 74-76HIBERNIA/PA5 Rev. F. Received: 22/07/2025. J874 01 Rev A, J874 02 Rev A, J874 03 Rev A. Received: 31/07/2025) therewith and approved by the Local Planning Authority, or as shall have been otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the buildings are used. 
Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 4 - The building shall be only be used for public worship and religious instruction use (under Class F1(f)) and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Class F1 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes)) Order 1987 (as amended), nor in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification. 
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby uses and the character of the area.

Condition : 5 - No classes or any other social events (excluding public worship) shall be carried out outside the following times: 8:00am to 9:00pm on Monday to Friday and 9:00am to 9:00pm on Saturday, Sunday and Public and Bank Holidays. No amplified sound (oratory or soundtrack) shall be played outside the premises in association with the permitted use. 
Unless otherwise first agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority, no amplified sound (oratory or soundtrack) shall be played that is audible outside the premises at any time and the doors to the premises shall be kept shut at all times other than for access. 
Reason: To protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 6 - Before the development hereby permitted is brought into use, the existing vehicular access to Hibernia Road shall be permanently closed and the kerb and footway reinstated, so that it cannot be used as an access across the pavement. 
Reason: To enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.

Condition : 7 - Cycle parking facilities (for not less than 12 bicycles) for visitors to the premises shall be installed to the front of the site. The approved facilities shall conform to the current Westtrans West London Cycle Parking Guidance (or such other guidance as shall supersede it) in design and layout and be fully implemented and made available for use before the first occupation of the development or commencement of the approved use as appropriate and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 8 - Within three months of the date of this decision, the applicant shall submit an events management strategy for approval to the Local Planning Authority that it will thereafter put into effect and update to respond to any issues that arise, as necessary. The events management strategy shall include an events schedule and event management measures to encourage visitors to disperse from the adjoining street without unnecessary delay after any event that they have attended and to do so quietly and without causing unnecessary disturbance for nearby residents (for example by avoiding littering, shouting or noise from the use of vehicles in surrounding streets) so far as the applicant is able to achieve this. 
The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved events management strategy (or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) and shall be maintained as such for the duration of the use. 
Reason: To protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 9 - The applicant shall inform the Local Planning Authority in writing at least one month before any large events (including festival events) that are intended to attract more than the usual daily worship attendance numbers and in advance of any event planned to be held at the site that exceeds the submitted 'Events and Visitor Numbers Information'. The event shall proceed in accordance with the 'events management strategy' referred to in Condition 8 or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) and shall be maintained as such for the duration of the use. 
Reason: To protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 10 - Within three months of the date of this decision, the applicant shall submit for approval by the Local Planning Authority a travel plan in accordance with current Council and TfL guidance comprising immediate, continuing and long-term measures to promote and encourage a reduction in car use shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved travel plan shall be implemented upon occupation and thereafter monitored and reviewed in accordance with the agreed travel plan targets and timescales to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
